sections.heading: C — Graduated licensing for drivers under 18, provisional licensee rules and restrictions (North Carolina)
sections.markdown:
## C — Graduated licensing for drivers under 18, provisional licensee rules and restrictions (North Carolina)
Knowledge domain: the three graduated licensing levels for teens, the rules every provisional licensee follows, and what a license restriction means.

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
The Level One Limited Learner Permit is for North Carolina residents at least 15 but under 18 who will drive vehicles needing a Class C license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
Before taking the permit test, a teen must show a certificate for an approved driver education course with at least 30 hours in the classroom and six hours behind the wheel. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
A Level One applicant must pass the written, sign and vision tests. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
For the first six months, a Level One permit holder may drive only from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., and only with the supervising driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
Once six months have passed since Level One was issued, the holder may drive at any hour, still with a supervising driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
A teen must keep the Level One permit for nine months before applying for the Limited Provisional License. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
The Level One driving log must record at least 60 hours behind the wheel, with at least 10 of those hours at night. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
For the log, daytime driving means sunrise to sunset while there is daylight, and night driving means after sunset when there is no daylight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
The supervising driver signs the driving log, and it is turned in to the Division when the teen applies for the Limited Provisional License. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
With a Level One permit, every passenger must wear a seat belt or ride in a child safety seat, and only the driver and the supervising driver may sit in front. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A01
A Level One driver may not use a cell phone or any connected cell-phone technology while driving on a public street, highway or public vehicular area. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A01
The only cell phone exception for a teen driver is an emergency call to an emergency operator, a hospital, doctor's office or clinic, an ambulance service, a fire department, a law enforcement agency, or a parent, legal guardian or spouse. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A01
To move up to Level Two, the teen must have had no moving violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions during the previous six months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A01
A supervising driver must be a parent, grandparent or guardian, or a responsible adult the parent or guardian approves, and must hold a valid license that has been held for at least five years. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
The Level Two Limited Provisional License is for drivers at least 16 but under 18. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
A Level Two driver may drive alone from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., and at any hour when going straight to or from work or a volunteer fire, rescue or emergency medical service they belong to. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A02
A teen must hold the Level Two license for at least six months before applying for the Full Provisional License. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A02
At Level Two, all passengers must be belted or in a child safety seat, and when supervision is required the supervising driver sits beside the driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A02
When driving unsupervised at Level Two, a driver may carry one passenger under twenty-one from outside the household, plus one additional outside passenger under twenty-one who is a student being driven directly to or from school, while there is no under-twenty-one limit when all passengers live in the driver's household [A02].
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A02
One additional under-21 passenger from outside the household is allowed only when that passenger is a student being driven directly to or from school. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A02
When driving unsupervised at Level Two, there is no under-twenty-one passenger limit if every passenger lives in the driver's household, but under-twenty-one household members may not ride in the vehicle while under-twenty-one non-household members are aboard [A02].
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A02
Level Two drivers face the same cell phone ban and the same short list of emergency-call exceptions as Level One drivers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A02
To move up to Level Three, the driver must have had no moving violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions in the previous six months. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A02
An eligible driver can upgrade from Level Two to the Level Three Full Provisional License online, and can upgrade to a regular Class C license online at age 18. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A02
A Full Provisional License drops the Level One and Level Two limits on driving hours, supervision and passengers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A02
A Full Provisional licensee who is still under 18 may not use a cell phone while driving, apart from the same emergency calls. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A03
A new North Carolina resident aged 15 to 17 who holds a permit or license from elsewhere should contact a local driver license office to learn which permit or license they qualify for. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A03
Every driver under 18 is a provisional licensee, and special laws apply because this group has a much higher crash rate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A03
A driver under 18 must show the driver education certificate, at least 30 classroom hours and six behind-the-wheel hours, before testing for either a learner permit or a license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A03
The DMV watches a provisional licensee's driving record more closely and may contact the driver after certain convictions or crashes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A03
A provisional licensee may not drive after or while consuming any amount of alcohol or drugs, and a conviction brings a one-year license revocation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A03
A parent or legal guardian must sign for a minor's permit or license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A03
A provisional licensee may not use a cellphone, type multiple letters or text to communicate, or read email or text messages while driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A03
Everyone riding in a moving vehicle driven by a provisional licensee must have a seat belt properly fastened. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A04
A student loses their license if suspended from school for more than 10 days in a row, or sent to an alternative educational setting for discipline for more than 10 days in a row, and the loss lasts 12 months. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A04
A license can be restricted for safety, for example to driving only while wearing corrective lenses or only with equipment needed to drive safely. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A04
A driver who goes outside the limits of a license restriction is treated as driving without a license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A04
The DMV may copy your documents or hold them briefly to check that they are genuine, and it rejects any document that shows alteration. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A04
A first-time North Carolina applicant must prove full name and date of birth, North Carolina residence address, and a Social Security number or legal presence in the U.S. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A04
Applicants for a driver license must also show proof of vehicle liability insurance. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F41 | anchor: A04
A North Carolina card marked Not for Federal Identification is still a valid state license, permit or ID. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F42 | anchor: A04
Beginning May 7, 2025, holders of a Not for Federal Identification card need extra documents to board commercial flights or enter federal facilities, military bases or nuclear power plants that require identification. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

Misconceptions: Level One night limits end after six months but supervision does not; Level Two still requires supervision outside the unsupervised hours; any amount of alcohol counts for a provisional licensee, not just a legal limit; the Full Provisional License removes hour and passenger limits but not the under-age cell phone ban.
Mnemonics: the three levels run Permit, Provisional, Full — learn with an adult, drive alone by day, then drive freely; the phone rule is No Phone except an Emergency call.
Glossary: provisional licensee means any driver younger than eighteen; supervising driver means a parent, grandparent, guardian or approved adult with a long-held license; driving log means the signed record of supervised practice hours; restriction means a limit printed on a license.
Dynamic facts: the federal-identification document date and online upgrade availability are policy details that can change and are isolated as dynamic; confirm on the DMV website.

items.skill: graduated licensing level rules (hours, passengers, holding periods)
items.why: three levels with overlapping but different hour, supervision and passenger limits are a classic confusable set best drilled as scenarios

corpus_stability.reason: The handbook prints a single revision date (Revised May 2025) on its back cover and states laws and fees are subject to change by the General Assembly; no sign of more than one revision per year in the selected pages.
